name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH11_MATCH_Q01 - Enzymes used in DNA isolation

questiontext.text:
Match the enzymes in List I with their specific targets during the isolation of pure DNA, and select the correct combination.

List I (Enzyme)List II (Target / Role)
(A) Lysozyme(i) Removal of RNA
(B) Cellulase(ii) Fungal cell wall
(C) Chitinase(iii) Bacterial cell wall
(D) Ribonuclease(iv) Plant cell wall

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
To obtain pure DNA free from other macromolecules, cells must be lysed using wall-degrading enzymes specific to the organism, followed by enzymatic removal of contaminating RNA and proteins.

Step 2: Individual Pairings
Lysozyme digests the peptidoglycan cell wall of bacteria. Cellulase breaks down the cellulose cell wall of plant cells. Chitinase degrades the chitinous cell wall of fungi. Ribonuclease (RNase) hydrolyses RNA molecules so they are separated from the DNA.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Thus, lysozyme pairs with bacterial cell wall, cellulase with plant cell wall, chitinase with fungal cell wall, and ribonuclease with removal of RNA, corresponding to (A)-(iii), (B)-(iv), (C)-(ii), (D)-(i).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH11_MATCH_Q02 - Tools of recombinant DNA technology

questiontext.text:
Match the tools and techniques of recombinant DNA technology in List I with their primary functions in List II.

List I (Tool / Technique)List II (Function)
(A) Restriction endonuclease(i) Transfers alien DNA into host organism
(B) DNA ligase(ii) Separates DNA fragments according to size
(C) Plasmid vector(iii) Cuts DNA at specific internal palindromic sites
(D) Gel electrophoresis(iv) Joins cut DNA molecules end-to-end

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Recombinant DNA technology relies on molecular scissors to cut DNA, ligases to join fragments, vectors to carry the DNA into hosts, and electrophoresis to resolve DNA fragments.

Step 2: Individual Pairings
Restriction endonucleases act as molecular scissors that cut DNA at specific internal palindromic sequences. DNA ligase catalyses the joining of cut DNA ends to form a recombinant molecule. A plasmid serves as a cloning vector to deliver alien DNA into a host cell. Gel electrophoresis separates negatively charged DNA fragments by size through a sieving matrix.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (A)-(iii), (B)-(iv), (C)-(i), (D)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH11_MATCH_Q03 - Pioneers and foundational milestones in biotechnology

questiontext.text:
Match the scientists, enzymes, or organisations in List I with their contributions in List II.

List IList II
(A) Herbert Boyer(i) First restriction endonuclease recognising a 6-bp sequence
(B) Stanley Cohen(ii) Defined biotechnology integrating natural science and organisms
(C) Hind II(iii) Observed sticky ends produced by E. coli restriction enzymes
(D) EFB(iv) Developed method to remove and reinsert bacterial plasmids

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Modern biotechnology emerged from foundational discoveries in restriction enzymology, plasmid biology, and formal definitions integrating traditional and molecular approaches.

Step 2: Individual Pairings
Herbert Boyer studied E. coli restriction enzymes and observed that they cut DNA to leave sticky ends. Stanley Cohen studied autonomously replicating plasmids and developed methods to remove and reinsert them into bacterial cells. Hind II was the first restriction endonuclease characterised, cutting DNA at a specific six-base-pair recognition sequence. The European Federation of Biotechnology (EFB) defined biotechnology as the integration of natural science and organisms, cells, parts thereof, and molecular analogues for products and services.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the valid pairing is (A)-(iii), (B)-(iv), (C)-(i), (D)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH11_MATCH_Q04 - Methods of introducing alien DNA into hosts

questiontext.text:
Match the DNA delivery methods in List I with their corresponding host systems or mechanisms in List II.

List I (Delivery Method)List II (Host / Mechanism)
(A) Divalent cations and heat shock(i) Bombarding plant cells with DNA-coated gold or tungsten particles
(B) Micro-injection(ii) Infecting cells using modified Ti plasmid or retroviruses
(C) Biolistics (gene gun)(iii) Direct injection of recombinant DNA into animal cell nucleus
(D) Disarmed pathogen vectors(iv) Making bacterial cells competent to take up plasmid DNA

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Because DNA is hydrophilic, specialised physical, chemical, or biological methods are needed to introduce recombinant DNA into bacterial, plant, or animal host cells.

Step 2: Individual Pairings
Treating bacteria with divalent calcium ions followed by heat shock at \(42^{\circ}\text{C}\) makes bacterial cells competent to take up recombinant DNA. Micro-injection directly delivers recombinant DNA into the nucleus of an animal cell. Biolistics, or the gene gun method, bombards plant cells with high-velocity micro-particles of gold or tungsten coated with DNA. Disarmed pathogen vectors, such as modified Ti plasmids or disarmed retroviruses, infect host cells to transfer recombinant DNA without causing disease.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Hence, the correct pairing is (A)-(iv), (B)-(iii), (C)-(i), (D)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH11_MATCH_Q05 - Genetic elements of cloning vector pBR322

questiontext.text:
Match the genetic elements of the E. coli cloning vector pBR322 in List I with their descriptions in List II.

List I (Vector Element)List II (Description)
(A) ori(i) Codes for proteins involved in plasmid replication
(B) rop(ii) Selectable marker containing BamH I and Sal I sites
(C) \(\text{amp}^{\text{R}}\)(iii) Sequence where replication starts and copy number is controlled
(D) \(\text{tet}^{\text{R}}\)(iv) Selectable marker containing Pst I and Pvu I sites

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
An engineered cloning vector such as pBR322 contains an origin of replication, replication-associated genes, and antibiotic resistance selectable markers with unique restriction sites.

Step 2: Individual Pairings
The origin of replication (ori) initiates DNA replication and controls the copy number of the linked DNA. The rop gene codes for proteins involved in the replication of the plasmid. The ampicillin resistance gene (\(\text{amp}^{\text{R}}\)) is a selectable marker that houses the unique Pst I and Pvu I restriction sites. The tetracycline resistance gene (\(\text{tet}^{\text{R}}\)) is a selectable marker that houses the unique BamH I and Sal I restriction sites.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (A)-(iii), (B)-(i), (C)-(iv), (D)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH11_MATCH_Q06 - Separation, staining, and elution of DNA

questiontext.text:
Match the reagents and steps used in DNA separation and purification (List I) with their specific roles (List II).

List I (Reagent / Step)List II (Role)
(A) Agarose(i) Precipitates purified DNA as fine threads
(B) Ethidium bromide(ii) Extraction of cut DNA bands from the gel piece
(C) Elution(iii) Natural polymer from seaweeds used as sieving matrix
(D) Chilled ethanol(iv) Stains DNA to appear as bright orange bands under UV light

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Isolating a specific DNA fragment requires precipitating bulk DNA, resolving digested fragments by size on a gel, visualising them, and recovering the target band.

Step 2: Individual Pairings
Agarose is a natural polymer extracted from seaweeds that provides the sieving matrix in gel electrophoresis. Ethidium bromide stains DNA so that bright orange bands become visible upon exposure to UV radiation. Elution is the step in which separated DNA bands are cut out from the agarose gel and extracted from the gel piece. Chilled ethanol is added during DNA isolation to precipitate purified DNA as fine threads for spooling.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The accurate pairing is (A)-(iii), (B)-(iv), (C)-(ii), (D)-(i).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH11_MATCH_Q07 - Polymerase chain reaction stages and components

questiontext.text:
Match the PCR stages and components in List I with their correct descriptions in List II.

List IList II
(A) Denaturation(i) Bacterium yielding thermostable DNA polymerase
(B) Primer annealing(ii) High-temperature separation of double-stranded DNA
(C) Extension(iii) Complementary oligonucleotides bind to template DNA
(D) Thermus aquaticus(iv) DNA polymerase adds deoxynucleotides to primers

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) amplifies a specific DNA segment in vitro through repeated three-step thermal cycles catalysed by a heat-stable DNA polymerase.

Step 2: Individual Pairings
Denaturation uses high temperature to separate the two strands of double-stranded template DNA. Primer annealing allows chemically synthesised oligonucleotide primers to hybridise to their complementary sequences on the single-stranded templates. Extension is the step in which DNA polymerase extends the primers using provided deoxynucleotides. Thermus aquaticus is the thermophilic bacterium from which the thermostable DNA polymerase (Taq polymerase) is isolated.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Thus, the correct matching is (A)-(ii), (B)-(iii), (C)-(iv), (D)-(i).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH11_MATCH_Q08 - Selection of transformants and recombinants

questiontext.text:
Match the bacterial colony types in List I with their expected growth or colour phenotype in List II.

List I (Colony Type)List II (Observed Phenotype)
(A) Untransformed E. coli(i) Grows on ampicillin medium but not on tetracycline medium
(B) Non-recombinant transformant with intact pBR322(ii) Produces colourless colonies on chromogenic substrate
(C) Recombinant pBR322 with insert at BamH I(iii) Dies on medium containing ampicillin or tetracycline
(D) Recombinant with insert in \(\beta\)-galactosidase gene(iv) Grows on both ampicillin and tetracycline media

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Selectable markers distinguish untransformed cells from transformants, and insertional inactivation distinguishes non-recombinant transformants from true recombinants.

Step 2: Individual Pairings
Normal untransformed E. coli cells lack resistance genes and therefore die on media containing ampicillin or tetracycline. A non-recombinant transformant carrying intact pBR322 retains both \(\text{amp}^{\text{R}}\) and \(\text{tet}^{\text{R}}\), growing on both antibiotics. A recombinant pBR322 carrying an insert at the BamH I site loses tetracycline resistance due to insertional inactivation, so it grows on ampicillin but not on tetracycline. Insertion within the \(\beta\)-galactosidase coding sequence inactivates the enzyme, resulting in colourless colonies in the presence of a chromogenic substrate.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Hence, the correct pairing is (A)-(iii), (B)-(iv), (C)-(i), (D)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH11_MATCH_Q09 - Large-scale culturing and downstream processing

questiontext.text:
Match the industrial biotechnology terms in List I with their corresponding descriptions in List II.

List I (Term)List II (Description)
(A) Continuous culture system(i) Separation, purification, and formulation with preservatives
(B) Simple stirred-tank bioreactor(ii) Increases oxygen transfer area using sterile air bubbles
(C) Sparged stirred-tank bioreactor(iii) Maintains cells in physiologically active log/exponential phase
(D) Downstream processing(iv) Cylindrical vessel with curved base processing 100–1000 L

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Commercial production of recombinant proteins requires large-scale cultivation in controlled bioreactors followed by purification and formulation before marketing.

Step 2: Individual Pairings
In a continuous culture system, spent medium is drained out and fresh medium is added continuously to maintain cells in their physiologically most active log/exponential phase. A simple stirred-tank bioreactor is typically cylindrical with a curved base and processes 100–1000 litres of culture. A sparged stirred-tank bioreactor bubbles sterile air through the culture to dramatically increase the surface area for oxygen transfer. Downstream processing encompasses separation, purification, formulation with preservatives, and quality control testing.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching is (A)-(iii), (B)-(iv), (C)-(ii), (D)-(i).
